A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP attribution research. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original attribution comparisons, grounding evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, object-discrimination results, and failure analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds numerical-integration and reference-sensitivity experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The integrated-Jacobian attribution procedure, straight-line integration, feature-pair decomposition, and attribution aggregation remain the same. The new pseudocode and alternative-reference experiments document and test the existing method rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO, Flickr30k, and HNC, including the same grounding, perturbation, object-discrimination, and hard-negative-caption tasks. The added integration/reference tests introduce no new reported dataset, population, or application task.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Interaction-CAM, InteractionLIME, both output- and hidden-representation ITSM variants, and the random perturbation baseline. ITSMout/ITSMhidden becoming ITSM-O/ITSM-H does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a protocol varying integration steps and four image/text reference combinations, measuring the discrepancy between Equations 2 and 10 and differences between attribution matrices. Existing splits, sample counts, five-epoch fine-tuning, metrics, and the default 50-step attribution setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 19–20 test numerical approximation as integration steps increase and attribution sensitivity to black/noise images and padding/empty text references. These focused checks supplement the retained perturbation, class-wise, hard-negative, and failure analyses.

E5.justification: V4 identifies previously unexplained shading in Figures 3 and 16 as standard deviations over evaluation examples and adds mean-plus-dispersion summaries of fine-tuning gains across models. Existing class-wise standard deviations and stochastic-dominance tests remain; no increased repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: Object discrimination revises positive actual-object attributions from 97.1% to 94.1%, and negative cross-attributions from 65.6%/70.1% to 68.4%/69.7% for original/fine-tuned models, with Figure 6 updated accordingly. V4 adds aggregate fine-tuning gains and convergence/reference-sensitivity findings. Tables 1–5 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds an O(D) time and O(D²) storage argument under its stated parallelization assumptions. Equation 13 corrects the right-hand integral's lower limit from 1 to 0. The main attribution derivation and reduction to Interaction-CAM are retained; separating the existing IG derivation into Appendix F is organizational.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its novelty statement: interactions in nonsymmetric dual encoders move from supposedly unexplored to almost entirely unstudied, explicitly acknowledging Joukovsky et al. The central claims about general second-order attribution, intrinsic grounding, mismatches, and domain effects remain.

C2.justification: V4 connects domain effects more explicitly to training-data contamination and strengthens the qualification that specific failure-case explanations should support hypotheses rather than definite conclusions. It also proposes discrete-text, nonuniform-interpolation, and nonlinear-path extensions. These are interpretations and future directions, not implemented method changes.

D1.justification: V2 promises future code release; v4 reports public availability and supplies a repository address. V4 also adds Algorithm 1, detailed Jacobian computation/storage discussion, and computational tradeoffs in Appendices I–J. This substantially expands implementation and access information beyond v2's existing explanation of PyTorch hooks.

R1.justification: Related work and discussion add focused literature on compositionality, distribution shifts, training-data effects, and IG extensions, including Lewis et al., Fang et al., and Sanyal and Ren. Earlier CLIP interaction attribution is acknowledged more consistently, while the fundamental positioning as a generalization of prior IG-based work remains.

P1.justification: V4 extensively revises explanatory prose across the introduction, method, evaluation, discussion, and conclusion. It creates a separate experimental-setting subsection, moves intra-modal details into Appendix B, and separates IG background from the Interaction-CAM discussion. These constitute substantial narrative and organizational revision despite stable core science.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains clearer grouping and a legend; captions, plot labels, and styling are revised. Figures 7 and 8 exchange positions, Figure 13 removes its OpenCLIP curves, and several displays relocate. Figures 19–20 and Algorithm 1 are added, while the established table structures and most visualizations remain.

improvement.justification: V4 improves assessment and reproducibility documentation through integration/reference checks, concrete code-access information, and computational details. It also corrects the novelty framing and clarifies limitations. The principal benchmark evidence remains unchanged. Algorithm 1 still has inconsistencies, including omission of Equation 9's 1/N normalization, which limits the implementation-documentation gain; overall, the improvements are useful but incremental.
